title: Strategic evacuation schedule and autoscaler coordination for Dedicated GPU fleets
creator: Maya Chen
description: Goal: Implement a capacity-safe, observable, and reversible evacuation protocol for Dedicated GPU nodes to support rolling runtime upgrades and LTS channel promotions. Scope covers the orchestration layer (controller changes), autoscaler handshakes, cordon/evacuation pacing, and operator playbooks. Out of scope: model binary conversion and per-model kernel selection logic (handled by runtime team). This ticket unifies a predictable evacuation schedule with autoscaler coordination to avoid capacity cliffs during upgrades and to preserve latency SLOs for high-priority customers.
acceptance_criteria: Can execute a staged evacuation (canary -> wave) across a single Dedicated GPU pool without violating configured latency SLOs for P50/P95 for the pool's routes (measured via canary traffic).

Autoscaler handshake API implemented: controllers call ScaleReserve(+) and ScaleRelease(-) signals to the cluster autoscaler and receive acknowledgements or a limited retry window. Confirmations are logged and surfaced in Console.
Evacuation pacing respects a configurable minimum spare capacity percentage (default 10%) and will abort/rollback if reserve falls below threshold before next wave starts.

Controller exposes per-wave metrics and a human-readable runbook in Console; on-call can trigger an automated rollback which returns drained nodes to service and restores prior autoscaler reservations.
End-to-end chaos test (simulated machine failures + API latency spikes) passes in staging with no customer-impacting errors for routes with priority >= 75.
plan: Design: define wave sizing, inter-wave wait windows, and reserve calculation formula (completed). See design doc link in attachments.
API: add Autoscaler Handshake endpoints (ScaleReserve, ScaleRelease, ReserveStatus) and decide idempotency semantics.
Controller: implement 'evacuation coordinator' that sequences cordon -> warm-migrate-prefix-cache -> drain tasks and publishes wave health.
Canary: run on a small subset of nodes (5% of pool) with synthetic traffic and metrics gating. If gates pass, continue with waves.
Rollout: general waves with automatic rollback triggers and manual approval step before last 2 waves for high-risk pools.
Observability: create Console dashboard panels for reserve headroom, per-wave latency deltas, eviction rate, and autoscaler acknowledgements.
Staging validation: run upgrade rehearsal with injected autoscaler delays and force eviction errors to validate rollback paths.
Docs & Runbook: publish operator playbook and incident checklist; add to weekly on-call rotation training.
decisions: Use 'reserve percentage' model instead of fixed buffer nodes to accommodate heterogeneous pools and varying instance sizes.
Make Autoscaler Handshake synchronous with a bounded timeout (30s) and exponential backoff for transient failures; if handshake fails repeatedly, controller pauses and alerts.
Evacuation pacing will favor gradual prefix/KV cache warm-migration before pod eviction to reduce cold-start latency for stateful LLM sessions.
Canary traffic will be routed via the same routing layer used for customers (not synthetic local routing) to surface real routing regressions.
risks: Incorrect reserve calculation could starve capacity for live traffic, causing SLO violations.
Autoscaler latency or API failures could leave nodes in limbo (cordoned but not drained) and complicate rollback.
Edge cases with long-running sessions: aggressive evacuation may disconnect active LLM sessions leading to client errors.
Race conditions between multiple concurrent upgrades targeting same pool (e.g., Dedicated + infra maintenance).
mitigations: Require controller to fetch real-time tokenized request patterns before deciding wave size; conservative default reserve of 10% until first two successful upgrades observed.
Implement idempotent handshake tokens and provide a manual override path in Console with enforced safety checks and authorization.
Add session-drain grace window and best-effort KV cache replication to minimize dropped in-flight requests; expose per-session eviction reason in logs for postmortem.
Introduce a global upgrade-locking mechanism that serializes upgrades per pool; conflicts escalate to on-call.
comments: 2026-02-26 - MC: Started design iteration with runtime and autoscaler leads. Decided on reserve-percent model after simulation shows better headroom across heterogeneous fleets.
2026-03-01 - DA: Prototype handshake endpoints in autoscaler repo; initial behaviour is optimistic and requires idempotency tokens. Filed PR #411 (see attachments).
2026-03-03 - PM (Liam O'Neill): Reviewed canary gating criteria; requested explicit P95 regression thresholds and a manual approval step before the final waves.
2026-03-05 - SR (Sabrina Rao): Security reviewed manual override flow and recommended audit-log enrichment and RBAC checks. Added to runbook.

2026-03-08 - DA: Staging rehearsals completed for pool 'dedicated-us-west-2-g1' with injected autoscaler 10s delay. Observed 0.6% P95 regression during wave 1, within tolerated threshold. Proceeding to broader rehearsal.
qa_plan: Create synthetic workload that mirrors customer token distribution and session lengths; run on staging fleet with same node types.
Inject autoscaler API delays/failures and verify controller pauses and alerts as expected.
Simulate long-running sessions and validate session drain grace behavior and log reasons for eviction.
Run end-to-end canary then abort mid-rollout to validate rollback path and measure recovery time.
rollback_triggers: Reserve headroom < configured threshold (default 10%) during any inter-wave pause.
P95 latency regression > 20% over baseline for customer-priority routes during a wave.
Autoscaler handshake failure rate > 5% for two consecutive waves.
Manual abort by incident commander via Console after safety checks.
monitoring: Dashboard: 'Upgrade — Reserve Headroom' (shows real-time reserve % and expected buffer).
Dashboard: 'Upgrade — Wave Health' (per-wave P50/P95, eviction rate, handshake success rate).
Alert: UpgradeReserveLow (sev-1) if reserve < threshold for > 60s during upgrade).
notes: This ticket is intentionally conservative: first rollout path will enable manual approvals before final waves to build operational confidence.
Follow-on work: automate autobump of reserve for pools with high session churn; expose recommended reserve per pool in Console.
